AI FOUNDATIONS · FINAL PROJECT

Campus Dining Demand & Waste Control Tower

An AI planning team that helps campus dining managers reduce avoidable food waste without running out of meals.

ONE-LINE PITCH

Turn uncertain demand into a transparent, safer draft prep plan.

Project owner: Elaine · 2026
01 · THE PROBLEM

Tomorrow's demand is uncertain.

A dining manager must decide how much to prepare before knowing exactly how many people will arrive.

Too much

Overproduction creates food waste and unnecessary ingredient cost.

Too little

Shortages create substitutions, frustration, and a poor dining experience.

Too many signals

Sales history, events, weather, inventory, and expiry windows are hard to combine quickly.

Primary user: a campus dining operations manager who needs a defensible decision in minutes.

02 · THE SOLUTION

A decision desk, not a generic chatbot.

What the app does

  • Reads recent sales and waste
  • Adjusts for weather and events
  • Checks inventory and expiry
  • Suggests preparation quantities
  • Shows cost and risk

What it refuses to do

  • Place food orders
  • Change inventory records
  • Hide uncertainty
  • Promise demand accuracy
  • Skip manager approval

The product makes tradeoffs visible so a human can make the final operational decision.

06 · SAFETY

AI recommends. A human approves.

Observed defenses

  • 78% context confidence creates review
  • Soup is marked “use soon”
  • Shortage risk is visible
  • Approval is a separate action

Operational boundary

The system creates a draft only. Approval records a manager decision; it does not place an external order or mutate inventory.

Figure 3. MCP calls, agent reasoning steps, Safety Review, and the Human gate are visible.

08 · USER FEEDBACK + NEXT STEPS

What a real user suggested.

“Add historical user ingredient preferences so the system can make better dining decisions.”

How we would add it

Use opt-in, aggregated preference signals to estimate which meals or ingredients users are more likely to choose.

Privacy and safety

Do not expose individual eating history. Preferences cannot override allergy, expiry, inventory, or food-safety rules.

Next: test preference signals against actual choices and manager adjustments.

09 · TAKEAWAY

Less waste, better decisions.

Campus Dining Demand & Waste Control Tower combines MCP tools, specialized agents, scenario simulation, visible risks, and a human approval boundary.

The manager leaves with:

  • A draft prep plan
  • Visible assumptions and confidence
  • Meal-level shortage and expiry warnings
  • Projected waste and cost
  • A clear next action

The goal is not to automate judgment. It is to make good judgment faster and easier to defend.
